title: Rapfi Level 8 vs Rapfi Level 7
intro: Rapfi at Level 8 (Black) against Rapfi at Level 7 (White), the settings of Mistboard's two strongest Gomoku bots, from a dealt opening: Black's h8 and i8, White's g6, j9 and i10. The graph has a line for each level: its own estimate of Black's chance of winning at every position, searching 80,000 positions for Level 8 and 25,000 for Level 7. Rapfi also read every position again at a million positions; the mark ?? and the notes use that deeper reading.

judged.26: White blocks the lower end, f4. Rapfi wanted the upper end, j8. After f4 the deep reading finds a forced win for Black: whatever White plays, Black can make five.

comments.25: For the first 25 stones the deep reading calls the game close to even. Black's g5 makes three in a row on the diagonal g5, h6, i7 with both ends open. Left alone, it becomes four with two ways to finish, so White has to block one end.
comments.27: l5 makes four: h9, i8, j7 and l5 on one diagonal, with the point k6 empty between them. One more stone there would be five, so White must fill it at once.
comments.37: By here both lines are at 100%: both bots now see the forced five. Level 8's line got there at stone 32, Level 7's at stone 36, and the deeper reading at f4, stone 26.
comments.49: l3 does two jobs. It makes four in column l (l3, l5, l6, l7), which White must block at l4, and it puts a third stone in row 3 beside j3 and m3.
comments.51: k3 fills the gap: j3, k3, l3 and m3 are four in a row with the points at both ends empty. White can block only one of them.
comments.53: i3 makes five in a row, i3 to m3, and Black wins.
